sequencing_rationale: The model comes before the query language because a learner who cannot read a table's keys and relationships writes joins by trial and error. Single-table SELECT work precedes joins and aggregation so filtering and projection are automatic before cardinality is introduced. Constraints and normalization come after querying rather than with modeling: their cost is only visible to someone who has already queried denormalized data. Documentation is last because there is then a real schema to document, and it is the lesson that carries the pathway's office-tools competency. SCOPE ASSUMPTIONS: the intake description is truncated mid-word at 'practice queries inclu', so the list of query types the course was meant to cover is unknown. The outline assumes a standard first SQL course against a sample database: SELECT/WHERE/ORDER BY, inner and outer joins, GROUP BY aggregation, primary and foreign keys, normal forms up to 3NF, and schema change. Assumed out of scope: stored procedures, query-plan tuning, replication, and database administration. Which SQL engine is used is left open; the lessons assume ANSI SQL against any of SQLite, PostgreSQL, or MySQL.

proposed_competencies.competency_text: The learner can write SQL queries that filter, join, and aggregate data in a relational database.
proposed_competencies.rationale: Nine of this course's twenty hours are query authoring, and the only available tag (D2-S1-C04) is language-agnostic feature building; the catalog names no data-query competency anywhere, even though two courses in the pathway are database courses.
